text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The international community may abandon Albania if its politicians fail to reach an accord on electoral law, OSCE special envoy Franz Vranitzky is quoted as saying.
- National Front Party leader Abaz Ermenji says his party will not form a coalition with President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party.
- The parliament closed its doors yesterday, opening the way for early elections due on June 29.
- Vlore residents are still waiting for Vranitzky to visit the town, known for its strong opposition to Berisha.
- Two people have been killed by bombs exploding in their hands in the anarchic southern town of Vlore.
- A 120-bed hospital has been set up in the town of Vlore by Italian troops. It will serve both troops of the eight-nation protection force and civilians.
- Five Albanian officers who were badly burned when an ammunition dump exploded are out of danger. Ten other officers escaped with lighter wounds.
- A Greek customs office on the Kakavije border with Albania re-opened after it closed due to attacks on traders by Albanian gangs. The office could close down again if violence is renewed.
- A draft law on the state budget for 1997 has finally been adopted.
- A Greek citizen was killed in Vlore when he was caught in a fight between two gangs.
- The electoral law passed by parliament last night meets all requests presented by OSCE envoy Franz Vranizky in the May 9 contract.
- The Democratic Party has always won and will win in Tirana, the capital mayor Albert Brojka said.
